rounds.text: Batliboi Ltd is demonstrating exceptional top-line and bottom-line acceleration that significantly outpaces the broader stock price movement, with 5-year compounded sales growth at 24% and profit growth at 31% [E15, E19], alongside a massive 90% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21]. This disconnect is highlighted by the fundamentals-led signal showing that profit growth has outpaced 5-year price growth and exceeded 1-year price growth by 124%, proving the company is starting to outperform expectations while the price lags [E55, E56]. Furthermore, operations are exceptionally cash-generative, boasting a cash conversion ratio of 3.29x with operating cash flow reaching Rs 23 Cr and free cash flow at Rs 6 Cr for Mar 2026, ensuring that reported profits are fully backed by hard cash [E34, E35, E36]. The macro backdrop is highly supportive as the Capital Goods sector sits firmly in a tailwind with a score of +0.59, matching the company's strong recent sales growth of 22% YoY and positive outlook for upcoming quarters [E63, E69, E71]. Conceded: [E8], [E9], [E10], [E13], [E20], [E26], [E45], [E46], [E47], [E60], [E61], [E67], [E68].

Batliboi Ltd currently trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E ratio of 42.18x compared to the sector benchmark of 22.02x [E6]. This elevated pricing is further underscored by an EV/EBITDA of 19.92x, which substantially exceeds the sector benchmark of 12.26x [E11]. The company’s operational efficiency remains a concern, as evidenced by an ROE of 4.0% and an ROCE of 6.8%, both of which lag significantly behind their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E13]. Furthermore, the company faces rising financial pressure, with borrowings increasing to Rs 107 Cr from Rs 86 Cr in the prior year [E39], and there is a noted risk that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E61]. While the stock is priced for high expectations, a reverse DCF analysis indicates that the current market price already demands an earnings growth rate of 18.3%, leaving a negative margin of safety [E45, E47]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong recent sales growth [E17, E63] and maintains a healthy dividend payout [E59].

However, the price-to-book ratio sits lower at 1.79x compared to the sector benchmark of 2.4x [E7]. While return metrics lag sector benchmarks [E9, E10], fundamental performance is accelerating sharply with trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth at 29% [E17] and compounded profit growth surging by 90% [E21], vastly outpacing longer-term averages [E14, E18]. This fundamental strength is supported by a tailwind score of +0.59 in the Capital Goods sector [E71], whose sector median sales growth of 23.1% [E73] and profit growth of 21.5% [E72] validate the operational environment. Furthermore, the company displays exceptional cash backing, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 23 Cr in March 2026 [E35] and a robust cash conversion ratio of 3.29x ensuring profits are fully supported by cash [E34]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth reached 29% [E17] and profit growth surged 90% [E21], while operating cash flow hit Rs 23 Cr with a 3.29x conversion [E34, E35]. However, the bull's attempt to downplay valuation premiums is contradicted by a P/E of 42.18x versus the 22.02x sector benchmark and an EV/EBITDA of 19.92x against 12.26x [E6, E11]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 86 against the market price of Rs 88, yielding a negative margin of safety of -2.2% [E45, E46]. The reverse DCF reveals that the current price already prices in 18.3% earnings growth [E47], while longer-term profitability remains deeply suppressed with a 10-year median ROE of just 1% and a recent ROE of 4% [E26, E29, E68]. Finally, the bull's optimism on capital goods tailwinds [E71] ignores deteriorating fundamental quality markers, including decelerating earnings growth [E67] and a warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E61].
